Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question at that time. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; and Taylor Kim, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results may differ materially from these statements due to a variety of risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm thrilled to report on CloudForge's outstanding performance in the third quarter of fiscal 2024. We hit significant milestones this quarter, propelled by surging demand for our ForgeAI platform—the cutting-edge evolution of our AI-powered DevOps and workflow automation solution—and flawless execution across our strategic priorities.

Our attention this quarter centered on four critical areas: accelerating new customer acquisition, fueling MRR expansion, driving gross margin improvements, and refining our cost of revenue structure. In new customer acquisition, we saw robust net adds that bolstered our growth engine. MRR trends showed healthy acceleration, reflecting the stickiness of our platform. Gross margins expanded meaningfully, highlighting our scalability. And we made targeted efficiencies in cost of revenue to support sustainable leverage.

These achievements position us strongly as enterprises increasingly turn to CloudForge for AI-enhanced CI/CD pipelines, observability, and automation that deliver real ROI in today's environment. We're confident in sustaining this momentum and creating enduring value for shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to walk through the financials in greater depth.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we delivered a stellar quarter. Revenue reached $845 million, up 32% year-over-year. Our GAAP gross margin landed at 82.5%, and operating income came in at $210 million.

We remain committed to investing heavily in R&D to fuel innovation and broaden our offerings, including deeper AI capabilities within ForgeAI. Our balance sheet is rock-solid, with ample cash to capitalize on strategic opportunities like tuck-in acquisitions or ecosystem partnerships.

Let me drill into the details starting with gross margin, which exemplifies the scalability and premium margins baked into our SaaS model. In Q3 fiscal 2024, GAAP gross margin hit 82.5%, a 330 basis point jump from 79.2% in the prior-year period and 70 basis points better than 81.8% in Q2. Non-GAAP gross margin, stripping out stock-based comp and acquired intangible amortization, climbed to 84.2%—a 420 basis point year-over-year gain and 90 basis points sequential.

This reflects the leverage we're generating via our CloudForge platform, which enables AI-driven workflow automation for more than 15,000 enterprise clients, including Fortune 500 players in fintech and healthcare—much like setups at ServiceNow or Workday. Key factors driving this, along with minor offsets we managed:

Scale advantages in cloud infrastructure led the way, contributing about 200 basis points of the year-over-year gain. With ARR up 28% to $1.42 billion, we secured bigger volume discounts and committed contracts from hyperscalers like AWS and Azure. Hosting cost per seat dropped 15% to $2.18, thanks to reserved instances now comprising 72% of compute spend—up from 58% last year—and smarter multi-cloud approaches akin to Snowflake's, where such commitments lift margins past 80%. Plus, shifting 40% of workloads to our in-house edge compute cut latency over-provisioning and egress costs by 22%.

A favorable mix shift to higher-margin AI and enterprise features added 150 basis points. NRR stayed firm at 118%, powered by upsells to CloudForge AI Suite, now 32% of revenue versus 22% a year ago. These AI tools, drawing on models like Anthropic's Claude, boast over 92% margins since they're mostly pure software with low hosting needs. Meanwhile, legacy on-prem services at around 65% margins fell to 8% of revenue after sunsetting them in Q1.

By region, Americas (62% of revenue) reached 85.1% margins with mature cohorts and 4.2% annual churn. EMEA climbed to 81.3% from 77.8%, aided by GDPR-ready data zones in Frankfurt and Dublin that trimmed compliance hosting by 18%. APAC (16% of revenue) was at 78.9%, pressured by USD strength against JPY/AUD and startup costs for Sydney/Singapore centers—about 50 basis points drag—but improved sequentially via our Tencent Cloud tie-up.

COGS rose just 18% year-over-year to $148 million, lagging our 32% revenue growth, due to tight professional services headcount (now 12% of COGS, down from 18%) and CloudForge bots automating 65% of Level 1 support, slashing third-party costs 24%. Sequential COGS had some noise from a $4.2 million Q2 AWS credit, but normalized, margins still gained 40 basis points.

For Q4, we anticipate GAAP gross margins of 83% to 84%, with further gains into fiscal 2025 targeting over 85% non-GAAP as AI efficiencies stack up. This puts us ahead of the SaaS peer median of 79% per Bessemer's State of the Cloud Index, via zero-trust containerization pilots trimming hosting 5-7% more and Okta integrations boosting seat density and NRR.

These dynamics validate our model amid enterprises' focus on AI ROI, similar to margin boosts at Datadog and HubSpot.

Shifting to new customer acquisition, another cornerstone of our momentum and a top indicator for sustained SaaS expansion. At CloudForge, with our AI-centric DevOps platform—building on GitLab or Harness foundations but with CI/CD, observability, and generative AI code tools—we've prioritized footprint growth despite macro pressures, budget reviews, and AI buzz.

Headline: Q3 net new customers totaled 1,847, lifting our base to 28,450—a 26% year-over-year rise in adds, up from 22% in Q2, and 7.5% quarter-over-quarter amid our product launches.

These wins generated $18.2 million in net new ARR from expansions and deals—up 32% year-over-year, fueling 85% of our 118% net retention. MRR impact: $1.52 million incremental, averaging $825 per new customer. Overall ARR closed at $312 million, +38% year-over-year; MRR at $26.1 million.

By segment:

Enterprise (>$100k ARR): 142 adds, +41% year-over-year, $12.4 million ARR (68% of total), average ACV $87k on 3.2-year deals. Displaced BMC/CA in Fortune 500, wins like a top U.S. bank and European telco for AI Observability.

Mid-market ($10k-$100k): 1,256 adds, +24%, $4.8 million ARR. Freemium conversions hit 28% quarter-over-quarter via ForgeAI Agent for pipeline debugging.

SMB (<$10k): 449 adds, flat year-over-year, $1.0 million ARR, with AWS Marketplace self-serve up 55%.

Regions: North America 62% (1,145 customers, $11.3 million ARR); EMEA 28% (517, +35%, $4.7 million); APAC 10% (185, +48%, $2.2 million) via Alibaba, Japan/Singapore ramps.

Drivers: PLG upgrades with ForgeAI beta (40% of trials, 15% to paid in 30 days, like Linear/Vercel); outbound win rates to 32% via ABM and predictive analytics (18 Snowflake joint wins); ecosystem with Snowflake/dbt/Terraform (22% pipeline), AWS co-sell ($3.1 million ARR); tiered AI pricing upping deal size 14%.

Efficiency shines: CAC payback 11 months (from 14), LTV:CAC 4.8x. SMB softness from rates cost 2-3 points, but enterprise/AI offsets. Q4 guide: 1,900-2,100 net new, $19-21 million ARR, on track for 35-40% full-year ARR growth.

Next, our MRR trajectory reinforces the reliability of our recurring SaaS engine at CloudForge. MRR ended Q3 at $25.2 million, +28% year-over-year from $19.6 million, and +5.8% sequentially from $23.8 million—beating Q2's 4.2% sequential pace post-ForgeAI launch.

Breakout:

New logo MRR: $4.1 million (+42% year-over-year), average $28k ACV (+15%), mid-market surge, AWS/Azure partnerships, three 7-figure fintech wins for GenAI CI/CD.

Expansion MRR: $2.8 million (+12% sequential), NRR 118% (132% gross expansions minus 14% contractions); 12-month cohorts at 1.7x start via API extensibility, 40% faster time-to-value.

Churn: 3.2% logo annualized (from 4.1%), dollar 2.8%; 95% gross retention amid peers' macro woes like Zendesk.

Regions: Americas $15.1 million (+25%, 60% mix, Google Cloud co-sell); EMEA $6.3 million (+38%, 25% mix, GDPR AI wins vs. Harness); APAC $3.8 million (+29%, Japan NTT ramp, China watch).

Tailwinds: ForgeAI in 65% new MRR, usage pricing +20% expansions; vertical GTM (DevSecOps) win rates to 42%; Rule of 40 over 130%. Q4 MRR +30%+ year-over-year, new adds ~$4.5 million; full-year $105-108 million, 27-30% growth.

Finally, cost of revenue breakdown: Q3 COR at $148 million, +18% year-over-year but controlled versus 32% revenue growth, at 17.5% of revenue supporting 82.5% margins—aligned with 80%+ targets.

Hosting: 45% of COR ($66.6 million, ~35% up), multi-cloud (AWS 60%, Azure/GCP); EC2/S3 for AI/collaboration (S3 +40%), egress from CRM ties. Efficiencies: 25% Kubernetes migration (PUE 1.25), Graviton pilots (-20-30% inference costs like Zoom), reserved utilization 85% to 90%, intensity to 15.3% of revenue.

Support/success: 30% ($44.4 million, +22% year-over-year), 1,200 staff for 125% NRR, enterprise focus; EMEA higher (12% vs. 9% Americas) offset by LLM triage (40% tickets, MTTR <90 min, $5 million save).

Other 25% ($37 million): transactions 8% (Stripe/Adyen 1.8% blended +30% volume), royalties 7% (OpenAI-like AI), PS amortization 10%.

Hedging cloud hikes via multi-cloud/spot (15%); Q4 COR 16-17% of revenue with Cloudflare edge (-25% transfer), APAC sovereign clouds for $100 million TAM. Positions vs. ServiceNow 75%/HubSpot 80%.

With these trends, we're raising full-year guidance: revenue $3.55 billion to $3.60 billion, reflecting first-half strength and Q4 visibility.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. At this time, to ask a question, please press star one one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been transformative, acting as our primary growth catalyst this quarter. It drove over 40% of new trials and 65% of incremental MRR, with quick 15% conversions to paid in PLG channels. Upsell adoption pushed NRR to 118%, especially in enterprise where AI modules command 92%+ margins and larger ACVs. We've seen it displace competitors in DevOps stacks, landing multi-year deals and accelerating land-and-expand. Overall, it contributed roughly 25% to our 32% revenue growth, and we expect it to scale further with GA features next quarter.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion?

Taylor Kim:
Great question, Lisa. International is a massive priority, now 40% of our base. EMEA grew 38% in MRR via GDPR AI and DACH wins; APAC up 48% in new customers through Alibaba/NTT/Tencent. Next: doubling APAC sales headcount, launching sovereign zones in Japan/India, and co-sell ramps with hyperscalers. Targeting 45% international mix by FY25 end, unlocking $100 million+ TAM in regulated sectors like telco/fintech. Early pilots show 2x U.S. velocity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan.

Mike Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Churn remains low and improving: 3.2% logo annualized, 2.8% dollar, with 95% gross retention and 118% NRR. Strategies include AI-powered success tools handling 40% tickets, boosting NPS; vertical playbooks for fintech/e-comm; and proactive expansions via ForgeAI usage data. Economic caution hits SMB lightly, but enterprise cohorts churn under 4%, aided by multi-year contracts. CAC payback at 11 months gives buffer—we're prioritizing quality, targeting sub-3% long-term.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We're excited about our Q3 progress and steadfast in delivering robust results for shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
